title: LRU Cache
hints: You need two things in O(1): find a key, and know the order of use. One container cannot do both - combine two.
std::list<std::pair<int,int>> keeps (key, value) in order of use, most recent at the front. std::unordered_map<int, list::iterator> finds a key's node.
List iterators stay valid when OTHER elements are inserted or erased - that is why a list (not a vector or deque) works here.
To mark a node as most recently used: order.splice(order.begin(), order, it); - it relinks the node in O(1) without copying. To evict: take order.back(), erase its key from the map, pop_back().
